newsitem.title: UK: Scotland's Hearts FC raise five mln stg in placing.
newsitem.headline: Scotland's Hearts FC raise five mln stg in placing.

text.p: Scottish soccer club Heart of Midlothian FC, set to join the London Stock Exchange next month, said on Friday it was raising 5.06 million stg net through a share placing.
The shares have been priced at 140p each, giving Hearts an initial market capitalisation of 14.17 million stg. Trading in the shares will begin on May 19.
The Edinburgh-based club will use the proceeds to build a new stand at its Tynecastle Park stadium, install undersoil heating and reduce borrowings.
The board said it had no plans to use any of the proceeds to sign new players for Hearts, currently fourth in the 10-club Scottish premier division.
Hearts have won the Scottish league title four times and the cup five times but the game north of the border is largely dominated by the Old Firm of Glasgow rivals Rangers and AIM-listed Celtic.

Hearts chief executive Chris Robinson said that it was hard but not impossible to persuade institutions to invest in Hearts. "People tend not to see beyond Rangers and Celtic in Scottish football but we pointed out that we have a consistent record of qualification for European competition," he said.

Hearts reported a pre-tax loss of two million stg in the year to May 1996 on turnover of 4.34 million. The club had a trading profit of 271,000 stg but interest and writedowns of player registrations pushed it into the red.

Robinson said he was confident that revenues would grow significantly from 1998/99 onwards when a new television and sponsorship contract is signed. The existing TV deal is worth only 16 million stg over four years.
